Kuwait Public Holidays and Holiday Work Pay

The next holiday is shown first; then calculate what you are owed if you work on a holiday.

Prepared and reviewed by the Mustahaqati team · Last updated: 2026-11-03

Pay for working on a public holiday

Public holidays in Kuwait: 2026 and 2027

HolidayDaysRest of 20262027
New Year's Day1 day—Fri 1 Jan
Isra and Mi'raj1 day—Tue 5 Jan; Sat 25 Dec (or Wed 6 Jan; Sun 26 Dec) · expected
National Day1 day—Thu 25 Feb
Liberation Day1 day—Fri 26 Feb
Eid al-Fitr3 days—Tue 9 Mar – Thu 11 Mar (or Wed 10 Mar – Fri 12 Mar) · expected
Arafat Day1 day—Sat 15 May (or Sun 16 May) · expected
Eid al-Adha3 days—Sun 16 May – Tue 18 May (or Mon 17 May – Wed 19 May) · expected
Islamic New Year1 day—Sun 6 Jun · expected
Prophet's Birthday1 day—Sat 14 Aug (or Sun 15 Aug) · expected

Pay for working on a holiday

If the work requires an employee to work on one of these days, they are entitled to double pay for the day plus a substitute day (Article 68). We calculate the day's wage as total pay ÷ 26 and the amount owed as twice that on top of salary, as published legal columns read it. Another reading treats "double" as including the holiday pay already in salary, so the extra would be one day's wage.

Example: total salary KD 800 and one working day on Eid: 800 ÷ 26 = 30.77, so you are owed KD 61.54 plus a day off. On the minimum reading it is 30.77, and dividing salary by 30 gives 53.33.

Holidays that fall on the rest day

The law gives the private sector no day in lieu when a holiday falls on the weekly rest day. The Cabinet sets linking rest days for the government sector for each occasion, and they do not apply to the private sector by law.

2027 holidays

No private-sector holidays remain in 2026. In 2027 Isra and Mi'raj comes twice (around 5 January and 25 December), and National Day and Liberation Day fall on Thursday and Friday 25–26 February.

Hijri dates are expected by the Umm al-Qura calendar and may move by a day; the Cabinet announces holidays before each occasion.

Frequently asked questions

How many public holidays are there in Kuwait?

13 paid days for the private sector (Article 68): the Islamic New Year, Isra and Mi'raj, Eid al-Fitr (3 days), Arafat Day, Eid al-Adha (3 days), the Prophet's Birthday, National Day on 25 February, Liberation Day on 26 February and New Year's Day.

How much is pay for working on a public holiday in Kuwait?

Double pay for the day plus a substitute day (Article 68). We calculate 2 × the day's wage on top of salary (total ÷ 26); the minimum reading is one day's wage on top of salary. Example: total KD 800: 2 × 30.77 = KD 61.54 plus a day off.

Why is Isra and Mi'raj a holiday twice in 2027?

Because 27 Rajab falls twice in calendar year 2027: around 5 January (1448H) and around 25 December (1449H), so private-sector holidays in 2027 total 14 days.

Does the private sector get the extra rest days the government gets?

The law does not provide for them; rest days linking a holiday to the weekend are Cabinet decisions for the government sector.
